title: Diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence to identify deeply invasive colorectal cancer on non-magnified plain endoscopic images
summary: A fine-tuned ResNet-50 computer-aided diagnosis system classified deeply invasive T1b colorectal cancer from non-magnified endoscopic images. In a third-hospital test set of 44 lesions, it outperformed novice readers on specificity but was slightly below expert readers. The authors did not test real-time colonoscopy.
ai_technology: A pretrained ResNet-50 CNN is fine-tuned to estimate the probability that an endoscopic image depicts deeply invasive T1b colorectal cancer.
organization: University of Tokyo; National Cancer Center Hospital East

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Third-hospital lesion-level evaluation reported AUC 0.888; at the study threshold, specificity was 87%, sensitivity 81% and accuracy 84%. The cohort contained 44 lesions.
evidence.unknown: Small retrospective test set; performance was below experts and no real-time or clinical-outcome evaluation was performed.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained ResNet-50 CNN is fine-tuned to estimate the probability that an endoscopic image depicts deeply invasive T1b colorectal cancer.
